body.statement: For either normalized two-arm contrast \(c\in\{(1,-1),(-1,1)\}\), one has \(S_c=\{1,2\}\), \(q^\star=(1/2,1/2)\), and \(V_c(s_c/2)=1\). The universal formula therefore reduces to \(R_n(c)=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), exactly the expansion in Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorem 3.1. This equality is the bridge from the published two-arm component to the new at-least-three-active-arm component of Theorem 1.
body.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check on the coefficient normalization and Airy scaling.
body.gap: This proposition reproduces the published scalar special case and is not claimed as a novel theorem contribution.
body.consumer: It lets readers audit the multi-arm notation and coefficient against the known two-arm benchmark.
body.proof_tex:
Consider first \(c=(1,-1)\).  Then \(S_c=\{1,2\}\), \(s_c=(1,-1)\), and the allocation definition gives \(q^\star=(1/2,1/2)\).  Put \(v=s_c/2\).  The response type \(t=(1,0)\) has \(b_t=v\) and \(\theta_t=1\), so \(V_c(v)\le1\).  Conversely, for any feasible representation,
\[
1=c^\top v=\sum_t\lambda_t\theta_t.
\]
Here \(\theta_t\in\{-1,0,1\}\), and hence
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t\theta_t^2
=\sum_t\lambda_t|\theta_t|
\ge\left|\sum_t\lambda_t\theta_t\right|=1.
\]
Thus \(V_c(v)=1\).  The same calculation after exchanging arm labels applies to \(c=(-1,1)\).  The cited unrestricted two-arm minimax theorem supplies
\[
R_n(1,-1)=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Arm exchange, together with negation of the estimator, is a bijection of the two design-estimator games and preserves squared loss, so the same expansion holds for \((-1,1)\).  Since \(V_c(s_c/2)=1\), this is exactly the specialization of the universal coefficient formula.
